script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only. Base case is a competitive, run-involved game: both fronts allow 4.13 YPC (JAX) and 4.30 YPC (NE), both blitz (JAX 39%, NE 38%), and the QB who has handled pressure is Maye (+0.09 EPA vs blitz, n=22) while Lawrence is -0.40 EPA vs blitz (n=10) and +0.42 when not blitzed. NE moves with Stevenson (24 carries/94) and Henderson (16/76) plus Maye scrambles (9/67); JAX leans on Tuten (28/131) when Washington's 279 air yards cannot be cashed.
script.flip1: NE's 38% blitz wrecks Lawrence, JAX falls behind, Tuten's 14-carry pace dies, and Washington's 18 targets become empty volume against a defense that has allowed only 4 passes of 20+ on 70 attempts. NE then clocks it with Stevenson and Henderson.
script.flip2: JAX keeps Lawrence clean, Washington (181 yards, 279 air) and Thomas (126 air yards on 11 targets) hit explosives NE has mostly denied, NE trails and shelves the Stevenson run, and the NE offense becomes Maye scrambles plus Doubs shots (151 air yards on 7 targets).

matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone charting are not in the pack. Location proxy only: JAX allows 7.86 YPA left (28 att), 19.0 middle (7 att), 7.78 right (18 att), with 8 of 58 passes at 20+. NE allows 4.48 left (23), 10.69 middle (13), 5.18 right (28), with only 4 of 70 passes at 20+.
matchup.pressure: Pressure rate and sacks are not in the pack. Blitz proxy: JAX 39%, NE 38%. Maye is better blitzed (+0.09 EPA, n=22) than not (-0.06). Lawrence is the reverse (-0.40 vs blitz, n=10; +0.42 with no blitz). A JAX blitz should not erase Maye's extension game; an NE blitz is the threat to Lawrence's deep shots.
matchup.bleeds: JAX bleeds the middle (19.0 YPA on only 7 throws) and explosives (8/58) and is ordinary vs the run (4.13 YPC, 5 runs of 10+). NE bleeds the run (4.30 YPC, 5 runs of 10+) and the middle (10.69 YPA) but not the perimeter or the deep ball (4/70 at 20+).
matchup.overlap: Usable overlap is Maye's already-shown rush role into a 39% JAX blitz he has handled, and Stevenson as the early-down/checkdown back (air yards -3) into a 4.13 YPC front and a middle JAX has not covered. Doubs (151 air yards) overlaps JAX's explosive leak but on only 7 targets. Washington's 15.5 aDOT overlaps the area NE has taken away, so that is a fade the 90.5-yard pace does not confirm.

form: Window is weeks 1-2 only; figures are totals, not per-game averages. Stevenson 24/94 (3.9 YPC) plus 8 targets/47 yards; Henderson 16/76 (4.8 YPC) with no target line, so the more efficient back is already taking carries. Maye 9/67 (7.4 YPC) is a real second runner. Doubs 7/96/151 air is explosive and thin; Douglas 9/29/44 is volume without conversion; Henry 8/66/69 is the TE. JAX: Tuten 28/131 (4.7 YPC) leads Rodriguez 12/36 and Abdullah 7/43; Washington 18/181/279 is the offense; Thomas 11/80/126 is quiet; Meyers 3/68/50 is 22.7 yards per target, a one-play look; Strange 5/40/51 is part-time; Lawrence 4/9 rushing is not a designed runner. No similar-defense splits are in the pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Maye has already rushed for 67 yards on 9 carries, about 33.5 a game, and JAX blitzes 39%, the look where his EPA is +0.09 on 22 dropbacks, so 27 rushing yards is under the role he has shown.
edge_players.must_be_true: He plays the full game, keeps about 4 rush attempts, and the JAX blitz creates escapes or designed runs rather than a spy that walls him off.
edge_players.kills_it: A contain or spy, a blowout that pulls him, or sacks instead of scrambles. If the 7.4 YPC was two broken plays, a quiet carry count misses 27.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Stevenson has 94 rush yards plus 47 receiving yards in two games, about 70.5 combined, against a 54 rush-plus-rec line, and JAX allows 4.13 YPC while the middle (19.0 YPA on 7 throws) is where his negative-air checkdowns live.
edge_players.must_be_true: He keeps a lead-back share near 12 carries and 4 targets a game and is not on a snap limit. Henderson's 16 carries at 4.8 YPC do not become the early-down job.
edge_players.kills_it: A Henderson takeover, or NE trailing so far that both the run and the checkdown vanish in favor of Doubs and Hollins shots.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so this is a form-and-matchup check only. Maye 67 rush yards in two games (33.5) is above 27; Stevenson 141 rush-plus-rec yards (70.5) is above 54. Both leans agree with the only numbers available. Neither is treated as a 70% leg: two-game samples and no spread. Washington under 68.5 was a lean the 90.5-yard pace disagrees with, so it was dropped. Lawrence under 16.5 agrees with 9 rush yards in two games, but NE's 38% blitz is a scramble threat, so it was not promoted.

market_rung_price: Maye rushyds over 27, price not in pack (listed +nan). Stevenson rushrecyds over 54, price not in pack (listed +nan). No alt rungs. Priced cousin not used as the leg: Stevenson recyds over 14.5 -115 is only the receiving half. No-vig comparison unavailable.
pre_mortem: Both lose if the two-game roles were noise and the missing spread meant NE was a big dog who never owned the clock. Maye over 27 dies if JAX spies the 7.4 YPC scrambler and the 39% blitz becomes sacks, leaving him near the 9-yard Lawrence pace instead of 33.5. Stevenson rush-plus-rec under 54 dies if Henderson's better efficiency (76 yards on 16 carries) becomes the Week 3 feature role, Stevenson is capped near 8 carries, and a snap limit or late scratch was invisible because no injury report was in the pack. The JAX middle at 19.0 YPA is 7 throws; if that was one busted coverage, the checkdown half of the Stevenson leg was never a funnel.
slip_story: One story: NE can function against a JAX blitz Maye has already handled and a front allowing 4.13 YPC. Maye rush over and Stevenson rush-plus-rec over win together when NE possesses, whether they lead (Stevenson carries, Maye still gets a few runs) or trail modestly (Maye scrambles, Stevenson checkdowns). Do not pair them with a JAX pass-over stack or a total under; those need the flip where NE's blitz stalls Lawrence or Washington's air yards cash. Tuten rush over 52 is the same soft-front idea for JAX but needs JAX not to trail, so it is a different slip.
